caption: A hairdryer is aimed at a bent plastic pipe, and the pipe softens enough to be straightened by hand and holds its new shape when cool.

sa.check: A hairdryer is aimed at the bend.
The pipe softens at the heated spot.
The pipe is straightened by hand.
The pipe holds its new shape.
The heating comes first, then the bending, then the holding.

pc.expect: The pipe goes from stiff to bendable at the heated spot and back to stiff as it cools, keeping its round section.
pc.fail: The pipe stays stiff and springs back as soon as the hands let go; or the pipe runs off as a liquid; or the pipe stretches like elastic while being straightened; or the pipe shatters at the bend.

pc.expect: The pipe holds the new shape once it has cooled and does not return to its old bend.
pc.fail: The pipe springs back to its old bend after the hands let go and it has cooled; or the pipe bends further on its own; or the new shape and the old bend alternate; or the pipe softens again with the dryer off and away.

pc.expect: The pipe bends only where the dryer has played and stays stiff elsewhere.
pc.fail: The pipe bends at a point the dryer never reached; or the pipe bends along its whole length while the dryer plays on one spot; or the dryer plays on the pipe and it stays as stiff as before to the end of the clip.

pc.expect: The pipe rests on its support and its free end hangs or is held; it does not rise.
pc.fail: The pipe lifts off the bench and hangs in the air; or the softened part bends upward with nothing lifting it; or the pipe floats toward the dryer; or the free end rises with the hands gone.

pc.expect: One pipe; it stays one piece and keeps its length apart from the bending.
pc.fail: The pipe breaks into two pieces; or a second pipe appears; or the pipe vanishes; or the pipe passes through the bench.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The pipe's colour, the dryer and the bench stay the same.
pc.fail: The pipe changes colour; or the dryer changes shape; or items on the bench rearrange.

note: The hands are kept because the straightening is the caption's action; they are otherwise not judged.
